example.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With Two Proportional Rows/Columns

question.text:
Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

\[ |A| = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 2 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & \sqrt{3} & 1 \\ -7 & 1 & -1 & -7 \\ 3 & 0 & \sqrt{3} & 3 \end{array}\right|, \qquad |B| = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 0 & -2 & 0.5 \\ 3 & -3 & \sqrt 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array} \right|,\qquad |C| = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 7 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & \sqrt{3} \\ 0 & 0 & -2 \\ \end{array}\right| \]
question.explanation:
Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn.

  • The matrix $A$ has identical columns: \[ A = \begin{bmatrix} {\color{blue}2} & -1 & 0 & {\color{blue}2} \\ {\color{blue}1} & 0 & \sqrt{3} & {\color{blue}1} \\ {\color{blue}-7} & 1 & -1 & {\color{blue}-7} \\ {\color{blue}3} & 0 & \sqrt{3} & {\color{blue}3} \end{bmatrix} \] As a result, $|A| = 0.$

  • The matrix $B$ has a zero row: \[B=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & -2 & 0.5 \\ 3 & -3 & \sqrt 5 \\ {\color{blue}0} & {\color{blue}0} & {\color{blue}0} \end{bmatrix} \] As a result, $|B| = 0.$

  • Since $C$ is a triangular matrix, we obtain \[ |C| = 7 \cdot (-1) \cdot (-2) = 14 \neq 0. \]

Therefore, only $|A|$ and $|B|$ are equal to $0.$

example.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With A Zero Row/Column or Two Identical Rows/Columns

question.text:
Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

\[ |A| = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{3} & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right|, \qquad |B| = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ \sqrt{3} & 1 & \sqrt{2} \end{array} \right|,\qquad |C| = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 4 & 0 & 0 \\ \sqrt{3} & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \end{array}\right| \]
question.explanation:
Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn.

  • Since $A$ is a diagonal matrix, we obtain \[ |A| = (-1) \cdot \sqrt{3} \cdot 1 = -\sqrt{3} \neq 0. \]

  • The matrix $B$ has two identical rows: \[B=\begin{bmatrix} {\color{blue}1} & {\color{blue}-2} & {\color{blue}2} \\ {\color{blue}1} & {\color{blue}-2} & {\color{blue}2} \\ \sqrt{3} & 1 & \sqrt{2} \end{bmatrix} \] As a result, $|B| = 0.$

  • Since $C$ is a triangular matrix, we obtain \[ |C| = 4 \cdot (-1) \cdot 2 = -8 \neq 0. \]

Therefore, only $|B|$ is equal to $0.$

example.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With A Zero Row/Column or Two Identical Rows/Columns

question.explanation:
Let's examine each matrix in turn.

  • Since $A$ has proportional rows, we obtain \[ A=\begin{bmatrix} {\color{blue}{1}} & {\color{blue}{-3}} & {\color{blue}{4}} \\ \sqrt 3 & -1 & 1.5 \\ {\color{blue}{3}} & {\color{blue}{-9}} & {\color{blue}{12}} \end{bmatrix} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \det(A) = 0. \]

  • For the matrix $B,$ we have \[ \det(B) = 2\cdot 3 - \sqrt{3} \cdot \sqrt{3} = 3. \]

Therefore, $5\det(A)+2\det(B) = 5 \cdot 0 + 2 \cdot 3 = 6.$

example.title: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With Two Proportional Rows/Columns

question.explanation:
Let's examine each matrix in turn.

  • Since $A$ has two identical columns, we obtain \[ A= \begin{bmatrix} \color{blue}2 & -2 & 2 & \color{blue}2\\ \color{blue}-1 & 1 & 0 & \color{blue}-1\\ \color{blue}1 & 1 & 1 & \color{blue}1 \\ \color{blue}3 & -3 & -3 & \color{blue}3 \end{bmatrix} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \det(A) = 0. \]

  • Since $B$ has a zero row, we obtain: \[ B= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 4 & 0 & 0 \\ \color{blue}0 & \color{blue}0 & \color{blue}0 & \color{blue}0 \\ 2 & 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \det(B) = 0. \]

Therefore, $\det(A)-3\det(B) = 0 - 3 \cdot 0 = 0.$
